items.title: For a family of finitely generated ideals covering the punctured spectrum of a local domain, the intersection is zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Let A be a local domain which is not a field and S a set of finitely generated ideals closed under products whose union of vanishing loci is the complement of the generic point; the lemma asserts that the intersection of all members of S is the zero ideal (statement lines 7343-7350). The proof is not a direct computation with the ideals but a compactness argument in the constructible topology: since the maximal ideal is not the generic point, some I in S is contained in the maximal ideal, so the intersection is contained in the maximal ideal; then for a nonzero f in the maximal ideal the closed set V(f) is covered by the V(I) with I in S, and quasi-compactness of V(f) in the constructible topology gives a finite subcover by V(I_1), ..., V(I_n) (proof lines 7353-7362). Because S is closed under products, the product I_1 ... I_n lies in S and V(f) is contained in V(I) for that single I; finite generation of I gives I^m contained in (f) for some m, closure under products gives I contained in (f^2) for some I in S, and then f cannot lie in that I (proof lines 7363-7367). Replacing a finite cover by one ideal through closure under products, and exploiting the two inclusions I^m subset (f) and I subset (f^2), is the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
